_meta.counting_rule: A legal entitlement, an execution rail, an adjacent alternative, and a rejected candidate are different objects. They are not added together as independent ways to move the same money. Cost grids are generated for every candidate so omissions are visible; non-executable candidates have blank costs and a reason.

categories.title: Personal legal entitlements
categories.description: Rights to purchase/remit CNY based on who you are and how the money arose.

categories.title: Execution rails
categories.description: Banks, card networks, cash and money-transfer operators used to execute an entitlement. A rail does not create a legal right.

categories.title: Business and asset routes
categories.description: Entity-level or asset-monetisation routes. They require a real underlying transaction, not a relabelled personal balance.

categories.title: Adjacent alternatives
categories.description: Lawful products or choices that do not freely repatriate personal savings as USD.

categories.title: Rejected / unavailable
categories.description: Prohibited schemes, unsupported corridors and common misreadings. No execution instructions are provided for prohibited schemes.

methods.name: Documented current-account RMB income of an overseas individual
methods.summary: A foreign citizen classified by the bank as an overseas individual may purchase and remit lawful current-account RMB income (salary, services, rent, royalties and similar) with identity, source-of-funds and tax evidence. The rule text does not impose the domestic-person USD50k facilitation quota on this documented route.
eligibility: Bank classifies you as 境外个人 under PBOC Order [2006] No. 3 Art. 37, normally by passport/entry-exit documents.
Income is lawful current-account RMB earned in mainland China.
You can prove the transaction amount and tax treatment.
pros: Direct legal basis for earned income.
No USD50k annual cap in the documented overseas-person income rule.
Can use a bank TT or an eligible provider rail.
cons: Old income may be hard to evidence.
PRC tax residence and U.S. worldwide-income reporting are separate questions.
A still-active PRC resident ID can create classification friction.
steps: Ask the bank to confirm your individual-FX classification in writing before moving funds.
Gather passport/ID, employment or service contracts, payslips/invoices, bank statements showing receipt, and tax payment/withholding records for the exact income.
Ask the bank for its current checklist for Art. 59 / PBOC Art. 13 purchases; obtain any missing tax certificate from the competent tax office.
Submit the purchase-and-remittance application for the documented net amount; do not describe savings as salary.
Compare the bank's executable CNY-to-USD rate, commission, cable and intermediary-fee treatment with another eligible rail.
Remit to your own U.S. account; keep the purchase slip, remittance receipt and tax records for U.S. reporting.

methods.name: Emigrant property transfer (移民财产转移)
methods.summary: A natural person who emigrated from mainland China may apply to transfer lawful property owned before obtaining immigrant status. SAFE approval is required; approved funds may be remitted once or in installments to the applicant's own overseas account.
eligibility: Foreign permanent residence, foreign citizenship, or HK/Macau/TW resident status.
Property was lawfully owned before the qualifying status was obtained.
Property is not restricted by judicial/supervisory authorities.
Hukou cancellation and overseas-settlement evidence can be produced.
pros: Capital-account route for a whole pre-emigration balance.
No USD50k current-account quota in the approval route.
Post-2014 rules allow one or multiple remittances within the approved amount.
cons: Only pre-status property; later earnings need another basis.
Tax clearance and identity/hukou issues can block the file.
Bank execution fees and FX are separate.
steps: Confirm the qualifying status date and make an inventory of property owned before that date.
Obtain foreign passport/ID or permanent-residence evidence, overseas-settlement certification/apostille as applicable, and PRC hukou-cancellation certificate.
Collect source-of-income and property-right documents for each asset, plus competent-tax-office tax certificates or electronic tax verification.
Prepare the written application and Individual Property Transfer Business Application Form; if using an agent, sign the agency agreement with both parties' ID numbers and date.
Apply to the SAFE office of your original household registration; respond to any correction notice.

After approval, take the approval document to the bank and purchase/remit within the approved amount to your own account in your country/region of residence. Do not withdraw the approved FX as cash in China.
Keep the approval, tax certificates and remittance receipts for U.S. reporting.

methods.name: Inheritance property transfer (继承财产转移)
methods.summary: A foreign citizen or HK/Macau/TW resident may apply to transfer lawfully inherited mainland property. The application goes to the SAFE office of the decedent's former household registration; multiple decedents may be combined in one application under the amended rules.
eligibility: Applicant is a foreign citizen or HK/Macau/TW resident.
Inheritance is lawful and documented.
Decedent's property rights and tax position can be evidenced.
pros: Combined applications for different decedents are permitted.
Approved amount may be remitted once or in installments.
cons: Inheritance and property-right evidence can be complex.
Not a route for your own non-inherited savings.
U.S. Form 3520 may be required for a foreign bequest.
steps: Establish legal inheritance with notarized inheritance/will documents or other accepted proof.
Collect the decedent's property-right documents and source/realisation evidence.
Obtain the competent tax-office certificate for the inherited property unless an exemption applies.
Prepare your foreign passport/ID, residence evidence, the application form and a written explanation of the relationship and inheritance.
Apply to the SAFE office of the decedent's former household registration; combine multiple decedents only as permitted.
After approval, purchase and remit through the bank to your own overseas account; retain all receipts for U.S. Form 3520/FBAR/FATCA analysis.

methods.name: Sale of mainland commercial housing by an overseas individual
methods.summary: An overseas individual who sells mainland commercial housing may purchase and remit the RMB proceeds under the property-sale foreign-exchange rules. This is distinct from an emigrant transfer of a pre-status balance and requires the property-sale chain and tax evidence.
eligibility: Overseas-person classification.
Lawful sale of mainland commercial housing.
Sale proceeds, original purchase and taxes can be documented.
pros: Can move sale proceeds rather than wait for annual quota.
cons: Property tax and transaction taxes may be material.
Local SAFE/bank practice and document checklists vary.
If the sale is part of emigration, choose the correct legal basis rather than double-counting.
steps: Complete the property sale and tax filings; retain the sale contract, title documents, original purchase documents and tax receipts.
Ask the bank/SAFE for the current overseas-individual property-sale purchase-and-remittance checklist.
Submit identity, sale and tax documents for the net proceeds.
Obtain any required SAFE approval/registration and purchase USD at the bank's executable rate.
Remit to your own overseas account and keep the full audit trail.

methods.name: Insurance proceeds paid to an overseas beneficiary
methods.summary: Where the insurance purchase was itself lawful and compliant, SAFE guidance allows an overseas beneficiary to purchase/remit insurance proceeds as lawful RMB income using the policy and insurer payment proof.
eligibility: Lawful compliant insurance purchase.
Beneficiary is an overseas person.
Insurer issues payment proof.
pros: Specific SAFE guidance for a real insurance payout.
cons: Not a savings wrapper; the underlying policy must be lawful.
Tax character depends on the payout.
Surrender values or investment-linked products may not qualify as insurance proceeds.
steps: Confirm the policy purchase and payout type were lawful.
Obtain the insurance contract, insurer payment certificate and beneficiary identity documents.
Ask the bank to process the payout under the overseas-person lawful-RMB-income rule.
Complete tax documentation and remit to the beneficiary's own overseas account.

methods.name: Reconversion of unused previously exchanged RMB
methods.summary: An overseas individual may reconvert unused RMB originally obtained by exchanging foreign currency, using the original exchange memo within 24 months. Small same-day amounts have simplified document rules.
eligibility: RMB is unused residue of a prior FX-to-CNY exchange.
Original exchange memo is available, or the small-amount exception applies.
Reconversion is within the 24-month memo validity.
pros: Restores unused conversion without proving new income.
cons: Only the originally exchanged unused amount.
Does not help long-held CNY savings without an original exchange trail.
steps: Locate the original exchange memo and match the unused RMB amount.
Present passport/ID and memo at the bank within 24 months.
For same-day cumulative amounts within the regulatory small-amount exceptions, ask the bank to apply the ID-only rule.
Reconvert and, if desired, remit under the applicable overseas-person FX remittance rule.

methods.name: Return of unused originally inbound foreign currency
methods.summary: An overseas individual may remit unused foreign currency that was originally inbound back along the original path. This is not a CNY-to-USD conversion route; it is listed to prevent miscounting already-FX balances.
eligibility: Funds are still foreign currency, not CNY.
Original inbound remittance can be traced.
steps: Identify the original inbound FX remittance and unused balance.
Provide identity and original inbound evidence to the bank.
Request original-path return of the unused FX.

methods.name: Domestic-person USD50k facilitation quota (identity-mismatch case only)
methods.summary: The USD50k annual facilitation quota applies to domestic individuals as classified by the bank. A U.S. citizen should not assume this is available merely because a PRC ID remains active; classification must be resolved first. The quota is a current-account convenience tier, not a capital-account savings export right.
eligibility: Bank lawfully classifies the applicant as a domestic individual.
Purchase is for a genuine current-account purpose within the quota.
No splitting or false purpose declaration.
cons: Not a general route for a foreign citizen's stuck savings.
Cannot be used to buy overseas property/securities as a capital transfer.
steps: Resolve nationality/PRC-ID classification with the bank and SAFE before using any quota.
If lawfully classified as domestic, complete the personal FX purchase application truthfully for a current-account purpose.
Purchase within the remaining annual quota and remit for the same genuine purpose.
Do not borrow relatives' quotas or split transactions.

methods.name: Above-quota genuine current-account expenditure
methods.summary: A domestic individual may purchase FX above the facilitation quota for genuine current-account expenditures with transaction-amount purpose documents. Tuition, medical care and similar real payments are examples; parking savings abroad is not.
eligibility: Genuine current-account expenditure.
Documents prove amount and purpose.
Purchase and remittance purposes match.
pros: No absolute USD50k ceiling for documented current-account use.
cons: Not a repatriation route for savings.
False invoices or purpose mismatch are prohibited.
Tax filing may apply to service payments.
steps: Obtain the real invoice/admission/medical or other purpose document showing the amount.
Complete the purchase application and submit purpose documents to the bank.
Pay the actual foreign beneficiary; keep purchase and payment purposes consistent.
Complete any outbound service-payment tax filing if applicable.

methods.name: Bank of China personal telegraphic transfer
methods.summary: BOC executes an outward personal TT after the underlying purchase/remittance basis is approved. Published commission is 0.1% of the CNY remittance amount, min CNY50/max CNY260, plus CNY150 international cable. FX and overseas charges are separate.
eligibility: Underlying entitlement approved by BOC.
Recipient and purpose comply with FX/AML rules.
pros: Optional USD full-arrival service for some intermediary routes.
cons: FX spread is not fixed by the tariff.
Full-arrival prepayment is not a guarantee against every downstream charge.
steps: Establish the legal basis with BOC (P01-P09 or a business route).
Request an executable CNY-to-USD quote and the TT fee breakdown: commission, cable, optional full-arrival, expected intermediary charges.
Confirm recipient name, account, SWIFT and address.
Submit the remittance instruction and supporting documents.
Track the SWIFT/credit advice and reconcile the U.S. credit against the quote.

methods.name: Bank of China foreign-currency demand draft
methods.summary: BOC publishes the same 0.1% min50/max260 commission for a draft plus actual postage. A draft is a physical instrument that must be delivered and collected; it is not an instant USD bank credit.
eligibility: Underlying entitlement approved.
Draft issuance and destination collection are available.
cons: U.S. bank collection policy must be confirmed.
steps: Confirm the U.S. bank will collect the BOC draft and ask its fees.
Establish the legal basis and obtain BOC's executable FX quote.
Request draft issuance; pay commission and actual postage.
Securely deliver the draft and present it for collection; reconcile final credit.

methods.name: HSBC China Premier / Advance telegraphic transfer
methods.summary: HSBC China Premier/Advance personal outward TT commission is 0.1%, min CNY100/max CNY500, plus CNY120 cable. Other institutions' charges and taxes are excluded.
eligibility: HSBC China account in the relevant segment.
Underlying entitlement and AML review passed.
pros: Global account visibility if you also bank with HSBC U.S.
cons: Advance account opening is restricted to specified customer groups from 2026-03-18.
steps: Confirm HSBC segment and any monthly service fee.
Establish the legal basis and submit documents.
Obtain executable FX quote and TT/full-arrival fee disclosure.
Send to your U.S. account and reconcile credit.

methods.name: HSBC China Private Banking individual telegraphic transfer
methods.summary: HSBC China private-banking individual outward TT commission and cable are published as free. 'Free' excludes other institutions' charges, FX spread and taxes.
eligibility: HSBC private-banking individual client.
Underlying entitlement approved.
cons: Not a legal entitlement by itself.
steps: Confirm private-banking individual status.
Establish legal basis and obtain executable FX quote.
Confirm whether any correspondent/receiver charges apply.
Execute and reconcile.

methods.name: HSBC Global Transfer to self-name overseas HSBC account
methods.summary: HSBC Global Transfer to a self-name HSBC account in an enabled country/territory is free for Private Banking/Premier; Advance actual charge is USD20 per transaction (CNY145 is only an indicative reference). It moves existing FX between HSBC accounts; CNY must first be lawfully purchased into USD.
eligibility: Both China and destination HSBC accounts in your name.
Global Transfer to Self enabled for the corridor.
Underlying CNY-to-USD purchase is lawful.
pros: Published Advance fee USD20; PB/Premier free.
cons: Does not solve CNY purchase entitlement.
FX conversion is a separate transaction.
Country/product limits and HSBC eligibility apply.
steps: Open/confirm self-name HSBC China and HSBC U.S. accounts and Global Transfer linkage.
Lawfully purchase USD in HSBC China under the applicable entitlement.
Obtain the CNY-to-USD executable rate and any conversion cost disclosure.
Initiate Global Transfer to Self; confirm the per-transfer fee for your segment.
Reconcile the U.S. credit.

methods.name: Wise CNY transfer funded from a Chinese bank app
methods.summary: Wise supports eligible non-mainland-Chinese individuals with China work/tax records sending CNY to their own overseas account. Bank-app funding limit is CNY300k per transfer and an overall net-income limit applies. Public quotes were observed but are not locked and do not verify a 40-point current fee schedule.
eligibility: Not mainland Chinese; HK/Macau/TW eligible.
Worked/work in China and valid tax record within Wise's lookback.
Recipient is your own overseas account or Wise balance.
Within per-transfer and overall documented-net-income limits.
cons: Overall limit based on taxed net income.
Current full fee schedule unverified; historical formulas not used.
steps: Complete Wise from-CNY verification with passport/ID and China tax records.
Confirm remaining overall limit and that the recipient is your own account.
Enter the CNY amount and choose bank-app funding; review the live fee and exchange rate.
Fund from your Chinese bank app within the CNY300k per-transfer limit.
Track the transfer and reconcile the USD credit; cancel unfunded transfers you do not intend to execute so they release limit.

methods.name: Wise CNY transfer funded from Alipay
methods.summary: Same Wise eligibility as R06, but Alipay funding is capped at CNY50k per transfer. No current numeric fee schedule was verified; the November-2024 formula is historical only.
eligibility: Wise from-CNY eligibility.
Alipay funding available and linked.
Within CNY50k per-transfer and overall limits.
pros: Alternative funding rail for small amounts.
cons: Same legal entitlement limits as bank-funded Wise.
steps: Verify Wise eligibility and remaining limit.
Choose Alipay funding and review the live fee/rate.
Authorize within CNY50k and reconcile the USD credit.

methods.name: Western Union China outbound cash pickup
methods.summary: WU China partner banks offer outbound cash pickup; bank-account payout is temporarily unavailable. The receiver must collect cash and then convert/deposit it, with separate compliance and fees. No numeric China-outbound fee schedule was verified.
eligibility: Partner bank accepts your ID and corridor.
Underlying FX/remittance basis approved.
Receiver can collect cash lawfully.
pros: Partner-bank online channels for some residents.
cons: Cash collection/deposit adds steps and fees.
Passport list excludes HK/Macau/TW passports; local restrictions apply.
steps: Ask a WU partner bank whether your ID, purpose and U.S. corridor are currently accepted.
Establish the legal purchase/remittance basis and obtain a live fee/FX quote.
Send via the bank's online channel or branch and receive the MTCN.
Receiver collects cash with required ID and declares/records it as required.
Receiver deposits funds; reconcile all conversion/deposit fees.

methods.name: Bank of China Great Wall debit card overseas ATM cash
methods.summary: BOC Great Wall card overseas ATM fee is CNY12 + 1% per withdrawal, max CNY112, plus any foreign ATM surcharge. SAFE caps overseas cash at CNY100k/person/year and CNY10k/card/day. This produces cash, not a U.S. bank credit.
eligibility: Own BOC card used abroad.
Within SAFE cash caps.
ATM network accepts the card.
cons: Annual cap makes large targets impractical/impossible in one year.
Foreign surcharge and U.S. deposit rules.
Future 2026-11-11 Mastercard/Visa pricing is not current on research date.
steps: Confirm remaining annual/person and daily/card cash headroom.
Use your own card at an overseas ATM; review the surcharge screen.
Withdraw within caps and keep receipts.
Deposit cash into your U.S. account following bank rules and declare cross-border transport if applicable.

methods.name: HSBC China debit card overseas ATM cash
methods.summary: HSBC China tariff: Premier at HSBC overseas ATMs free; Premier/Advance at UnionPay overseas ATMs CNY20 + 1%, max CNY110 per withdrawal. SAFE cash caps still apply.
eligibility: HSBC China debit card and eligible segment.
Within SAFE cash caps.
steps: Confirm segment and ATM network fee.
Check SAFE cash headroom.
Withdraw within caps, retain receipts, and deposit/declare as required.

methods.name: Carry foreign-currency cash out of China and deposit in the U.S.
methods.summary: After lawful conversion/withdrawal, cash export is permit-controlled: up to USD5k no permit; USD5k-10k bank carry permit; above USD10k generally not allowed except special cases with SAFE permit. U.S. entry/exit over USD10k requires FinCEN 105. BOC's carry-permit fee is waived through 2026-12-31.
eligibility: Lawful source and withdrawal.
Cash-export permit rules satisfied.
U.S. declaration and deposit compliance.
cons: Above USD10k generally prohibited absent special case.
Security, transport, deposit and declaration burden.
steps: Lawfully purchase/withdraw USD cash within bank and SAFE rules.
Determine permit tier; obtain bank or SAFE carry permit where required.
Declare cash to Chinese customs as required and carry permit/receipts.
Declare to CBP on FinCEN 105 if over USD10k entering/leaving the U.S.
Deposit at the U.S. bank with source documents.

methods.name: MoneyGram agent location from China
methods.summary: MoneyGram's China page gives generic agent steps but does not verify a CNY-to-USD own-account corridor, payout method, limits or fees. Treat as a candidate to verify with a local agent, not an available route.
cons: Generic page is not proof of CNY funding or own-account repatriation.
steps: Verification only: ask a MoneyGram agent in China for written confirmation of CNY funding, USD payout, own-account eligibility, limits, fees and required documents.
Do not send until the underlying FX entitlement and corridor are confirmed.

methods.name: PayPal C2 international payment
methods.summary: PayPal C2 supports international payments to accounts registered outside mainland China, but the checked page does not establish CNY bank-funded own-account repatriation or a USD withdrawal path. Unverified for this task.
cons: Payment to another PayPal account is not proven repatriation.
Funding, FX, withdrawal and fees unverified.
steps: Verification only: obtain PayPal written confirmation that a mainland CNY bank-funded payment to your own non-mainland account can be withdrawn as USD, with all fees and limits.
Do not treat a friends/family payment as a lawful savings-export route.

methods.name: FIE dividend to a foreign individual shareholder
methods.summary: A real foreign-invested enterprise may distribute after-tax profits to a foreign individual shareholder. From 2026-09-01 the old foreign-individual dividend exemption is repealed and 20% IIT applies, subject to any valid treaty relief. This is not a way to relabel personal savings.
eligibility: You actually own equity in the FIE.
Distributable after-tax profits and shareholder resolution exist.
Withholding and tax filing completed.
cons: 20% PRC withholding from September 2026 unless treaty relief applies.
U.S. dividend reporting and foreign tax credit limits.
steps: Confirm share ownership and distributable profits in the FIE accounts.
Pass a valid profit-distribution resolution.
Compute and withhold PRC IIT; assess treaty beneficial-owner/residence relief before payment.
Complete outbound tax filing if required and submit resolution/tax documents to the bank.
Remit the net dividend to the shareholder's account and report it in the U.S.

methods.name: FIE dividend to a foreign corporate shareholder
methods.summary: A real FIE may remit dividends to a nonresident corporate shareholder under direct-investment profit rules. The domestic reduced EIT rate is generally 10% for the specified nonresident income, with treaty analysis separate.
eligibility: Foreign company actually owns the equity.
After-tax distributable profits exist.
Withholding and bank registration/tax filing complete.
cons: Not available to an individual without a real company.
steps: Confirm corporate ownership and distributable profits.
Pass distribution resolution and withhold EIT.
Complete tax filing and bank direct-investment/profit-remittance documents.
Remit net dividend to the corporate shareholder.

methods.name: Registered capital reduction returned to a foreign investor
methods.summary: A foreign investor may receive proceeds of a lawful capital reduction after registration/change formalities. The 2024 capital-account guidelines contain a foreign-investor withdrawal-remittance section; detailed current document checklist was not fully extracted and is flagged.
eligibility: Real FIE capital reduction.
Company-law and registration steps completed.
Tax character of returned capital vs gain resolved.
cons: Current operational checklist not fully verified here.
steps: Complete the lawful capital-reduction resolution, creditor/publicity and registration steps.
Obtain the bank's current 2024-guideline checklist for foreign-investor withdrawal remittance.
Resolve tax treatment of capital return versus gain.
Submit registration/tax documents and remit to the investor.

methods.name: Sale of equity in a Chinese entity to a foreign buyer
methods.summary: A real equity sale can generate proceeds remittable under direct-investment/asset-realisation rules after registration and tax. It is not a device to move an unrelated personal balance.
eligibility: Genuine equity sale at arm's length.
Registration change and tax filing complete.
cons: Buyer and funds must be genuine.
steps: Execute a genuine sale agreement and complete registration change.
File and pay transfer taxes.
Use the bank's current foreign-investor withdrawal/asset-realisation checklist to remit net proceeds.

methods.name: Liquidation of a foreign-invested enterprise
methods.summary: State Council Regulation Art. 22 expressly allows RMB belonging to foreign investors of a lawfully terminated FIE to be purchased and remitted after liquidation and tax payment.
eligibility: FIE lawfully terminated and liquidated.
Taxes paid.
Remaining property belongs to the foreign investor.
cons: Entity debts/taxes must be settled first.
steps: Lawfully terminate and liquidate the FIE.
Settle debts and taxes; prepare liquidation report and investor distribution.
Complete deregistration and bank capital-account formalities.
Purchase/remit the foreign investor's remaining RMB under Art. 22.

methods.name: Genuine service or royalty export by a Chinese entity
methods.summary: A Chinese entity that actually provides services or licenses IP to a foreign customer may receive USD export proceeds. Service-trade rules require a real transaction; fabricated contracts are prohibited.
eligibility: Real service/royalty contract and performance.
Customer is foreign and payment matches the transaction.
steps: Perform the real service/license and document delivery.
Issue contract/invoice and receive USD into the entity's FX account.
Complete tax filings; convert or use FX under business rules.
Distribute any after-tax profit to owners only through a lawful dividend route.

methods.name: Goods export / individual foreign-trade operator / cross-border e-commerce
methods.summary: Registered individual trade operators, cross-border e-commerce and market-procurement traders may settle genuine export proceeds through personal/business FX accounts under the 2020 guidelines. Documented e-commerce/market-procurement settlement does not consume the facilitation quota.
eligibility: Real goods export and required registration/platform records.
Transport/customs/transaction data match.
pros: Quota non-occupation for documented e-commerce/market procurement.
cons: Requires genuine trade, not a paper export.
steps: Complete required trade/e-commerce/market-procurement registration.
Export goods and retain contract, logistics, customs and platform transaction data.
Receive proceeds through the permitted FX account and settle with documents.
Pay business taxes; distribute profits lawfully.

methods.name: Outbound intercompany lending or cross-border cash pooling
methods.summary: Group treasury tools can move funds across borders under registration/quota rules, but they create repayment/repatriation obligations and are not personal savings conversion. Detailed current pooling rules were not fully verified here.
eligibility: Multinational group with real entities.
Registration/quota and arm's-length terms.
steps: Verify current PBOC/SAFE pooling or outbound-lending registration requirements with the bank.
Document group relationship, quota, terms and purpose.
Register and operate the pool/loan; track repayment and repatriation obligations.

methods.name: QDII / overseas investment plan
methods.summary: QDII lets a licensed domestic institution invest domestic funds offshore within quota. It is an investment product, not a right to receive free USD abroad; redemption proceeds return through the product. Current HSBC subscription suspensions are flagged.
eligibility: Product open and quota available.
Investor suitability.
cons: Does not deliver spendable USD to your U.S. account.
steps: Check current product availability and quota with the institution.
Read subscription/redemption and repatriation terms.
Invest only if the goal is exposure, not repatriation.

methods.name: Greater Bay Area Wealth Management Connect Southbound
methods.summary: Eligible GBA mainland residents may invest in designated offshore products through a closed-loop RMB channel. Redemption/repatriation returns via the same route; it is not free USD repatriation to a U.S. account.
eligibility: GBA residence/permit and bank eligibility verification.
Product and quota limits.
steps: Verify GBA eligibility with a partner bank.
Open paired dedicated remittance/investment accounts.
Invest within quota; redeem and repatriate through the same closed loop.

methods.name: Registered employee stock incentive plan
methods.summary: A domestic agent and offshore trustee can operate a registered offshore-listed-company employee plan. Sale proceeds/dividends are repatriated through the dedicated account to the employee's domestic FX account; it is not a general offshore savings retention route.
eligibility: Real employment/service relationship and registered plan.
Domestic agent/offshore trustee and quota.
cons: Proceeds return through the dedicated structure.
steps: Confirm the plan is registered and you are an eligible participant.
Participate through the domestic agent/offshore trustee.
On sale/dividend, proceeds return through the dedicated account to your domestic FX account; use another lawful basis for any later outward remittance.

methods.name: Outward direct investment / special-purpose vehicle
methods.summary: ODI/SPV registration can move investment capital abroad for a genuine approved/filed investment. It creates an offshore asset, not personal USD spending money, and later distributions need their own basis.
eligibility: Genuine investment project and required approvals/filings.
Bank/SAFE registration.
cons: Project, tax and ongoing reporting burden.
steps: Verify current ODI/SPV approval/filing and bank registration requirements.
Document the genuine investment and source of funds.
Register and remit investment capital; treat later profits/returns under their own rules.

methods.name: Keep CNY in China or spend it lawfully in China
methods.summary: If no lawful outward basis exists, retaining CNY domestically or using it for genuine domestic consumption avoids an unlawful transfer. It does not achieve USD repatriation.
cons: Does not meet a USD goal.
steps: Do not force an unlawful transfer.
Use funds for lawful domestic purposes or wait until a documented entitlement exists.
Continue U.S. FBAR/FATCA reporting if thresholds are met.

methods.name: Splitting across relatives' or friends' quotas
methods.summary: Borrowing or lending facilitation quotas to evade limits/authenticity management is prohibited and can trigger the SAFE watch list. No execution instructions.

methods.name: Underground banking / matched off-book settlement (对敲)
methods.summary: Private or disguised FX dealing and unlawful transfer of domestic FX abroad are prohibited. No execution instructions.

methods.name: Crypto / stablecoin bridge
methods.summary: PBOC-led 2021 notice treats fiat/virtual-currency exchange business and offshore exchanges serving mainland residents as illegal financial activity. Not a lawful CNY-to-USD route. No execution instructions.

methods.name: Fabricated trade, service contract or invoice
methods.summary: Current-account rules require a real lawful transaction; fictitious trade backgrounds and false documents are prohibited. No execution instructions.

methods.name: Using the facilitation quota for overseas property or securities
methods.summary: The domestic-person quota is a current-account convenience tier. Using it as a capital transfer to buy overseas property/securities misstates purpose and is not a lawful savings-export route. No execution instructions.

methods.name: Relative's gift as a workaround for your own stuck balance
methods.summary: A genuine foreign gift may have U.S. Form 3520 reporting, but the checked sources do not verify a general PRC outward-gift purchase/remittance entitlement for a domestic relative. It is not a proven route for your own balance.
cons: U.S. reporting and covered-expatriate tax exceptions.
steps: Verification only: obtain SAFE/bank confirmation of the donor's lawful outward-transfer basis.
Assess U.S. Form 3520 and covered-expatriate rules before accepting a genuine gift.

methods.name: Revolut / Remitly / Xoom as China-outbound CNY rails
methods.summary: Checked provider/search material did not establish a mainland CNY-funded outbound own-account USD corridor for these brands. Inbound-to-China capability is not outbound capability. Unverified, not recommended.
cons: Risk of confusing inbound and outbound services.
steps: Verification only: obtain provider written confirmation of mainland CNY funding, USD payout, eligibility, limits and fees.
Do not rely on inbound-to-China marketing.

methods.name: Adding the U.S. 1% remittance tax to China-to-US costs
methods.summary: The U.S. 1% remittance transfer tax applies to specified physical-instrument-funded remittances sent from the United States. It is not a China-to-US transfer cost.
